data.author: khluu
data.summary:
v0.29.0
Highlights
This release features 594 commits from 277 contributors (91 new)!
Model Runner V2 is now the default for all models (#53183), completing the rollout that began with pooling models (#48290). MRV2 also gained CUDA graph memory profiling for KV cache auto-sizing (#53306), batch-sharded sampling that cuts per-step logits memory by 1/TP (#50465), prompt embeds (#42963), extracthiddenstates speculation (#49811), padded FULL cudagraph dispatch for uniform decode under spec decode (#53407), and DP-sync skipping before EAGLE/MTP draft prefill (#53694). MRV1 remains in use for a few ROCm models and features MRV2 does not yet support.
New models: Hy4-preview, Tencent's 770B/49B-active MoE with Gated DeepSeek Sparse Attention and native MTP (#54160); Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with BF16/FP8/NVFP4 and MTP (#53896); GraniteSWA and GraniteMoeSWA (#52706); NemotronHOmniReasoningV3 with MTP (#52929, #53121); Kimi K3 NVFP4 checkpoints (#53132).

data.title: huggingface/transformers v5.22.0: Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk)
data.author: LysandreJik
data.summary:
New Models
Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk)
Mistral Large 4 is Mistral's largest and most capable model to date: a 1 trillion-parameter natively multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with 49 billion active parameters per token (52 billion including embeddings and output layers), trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral's own datacenters in Europe.
Mistral Large 4 unifies instruction following, reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows in a single set of weights. While a generalist model, it shows especially good performance on workloads such as cybersecurity, finance, and law, and it surpasses frontier closed models on visual grounding. It is natively fluent in 160+ languages, including every official language of the European Union.
Key Features
Mistral Large 4 includes the following architectural choices:
1T total / 52B active parameters: granular Mixture-of-Experts with 128 routed experts (4 active per token) and 1 shared expert.
1M context length, for long-context workloads.
Multimodal input: accepts text and image input, with text output. Pixtral-style vision encoder trained to handle variable image sizes and aspect ratios.
Instruct and Reasoning functionalities with function calls, reasoning effort configurable per request.
Mistral Large 4 offers the following capabilities:
Reasoning Mode: three reasoning efforts — low, medium, high (default) — so the same model can answer a quick chat reply or work through a complex agentic run.
Vision: analyzes images, charts, technical drawings, and documents, with state-of-the-art visual grounding among open weights.
Multilingual: natively fluent in 160+ languages, including all official languages of the European Union.
System Prompt: strong adherence and support for system prompts.
Agentic: native function calling, JSON output, and strict JSON schema enforcement.
Cybersecurity: state of the art among open-weight models for security work, while refusing malicious requests.

data.title: huggingface/transformers Release: v5.21.0
data.author: Cyrilvallez
data.summary:
Release v5.21.0
New Model additions
MiniCPM-OCR
MiniCPM-OCR is a document-understanding model from OpenBMB's MiniCPM-V family. It keeps the MiniCPM-V 4.6 architecture, which pairs a SigLIP vision encoder and a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model. It is specialized for reading text-dense images such as scanned pages, screenshots, receipts and tables.
Links: Documentation | Paper
Feat test (#49920) by @guarin in #49920
Flint
Flint is Recursive's mixture-of-experts language model. Compared to a standard SwiGLU MoE transformer such as Qwen3-MoE, it uses hybrid attention (sliding-window attention with rotary embeddings over the current token and the previous 512 tokens in most layers, and full attention without positional encoding in the remaining layers). It also has learned attention sinks, as in GPT-OSS, with per-head RMS-normalized queries and keys. Each sparse layer routes a token to 6 of 256 experts by sigmoid score and adds an ungated shared expert, and the first two layers are dense.
Links: Documentation
Add Flint model support. (#49824) by @lovishmadaan in #49824
UltraVBert
UltraVBert extends ModernVBert by pairing the UltraBERT text encoder with a SigLIP vision encoder for visual document understanding and retrieval. Its image processor splits each page into 512-pixel tiles plus a global view. The connector merges each 4 x 4 block of vision patches into one token, so a tile becomes 64 image tokens, and RMS-normalizes them to the scale of UltraBERT's token embeddings. The maximagetiles setting (27 by default) caps the number of tiles per page.

Gradium Phonon TTS is Gradium's family of on-device text-to-speech models, trained with the Pocket TTS recipe. data.title: vllm-project/vllm v0.32.0
data.author: khluu
data.summary:
v0.32.0
Highlights
This release features 814 commits from 363 contributors (121 new)!
Structured decisions and generic parsers: the new POST /v1/systemone endpoint answers choice, noul and score questions over a structured state (#59299), is served by default (#60677, #60696), and also runs on Cloudflare/clef-omni (#61064), LiquidAI/d1-3B (#60676) and DiffusionGemma (#60466). The new hf tool and reasoning parser (--tool-call-parser hf, --reasoning-parser hf) reads the checkpoint's responsetemplate, so models that ship it need no model-specific parser (#58604, #58602), in both the Python and Rust frontends (#59005).
Low-precision KV cache everywhere: NVFP4 KV cache now runs on SM8x and SM12x (#46963), SM90 (#60620) and with XQA decode on SM12x (#60452), and on MiniMax-M3 sparse attention on SM100 (#59300); GLM-5.x defaults to an FP8 KV cache on SM100, halving KV memory per rank with 2.3-5.5% more throughput at a 7-11% TTFT cost in the PR's benchmark (#60140, #60281); fp8dsmla on SM90 gives GLM-5.3-Flash up to 31% more output throughput (#59246); ROCm gains the 4-bit ultraquant4bit KV cache with about 2x the density of FP8 (#57057).
Model Runner V2: a GPU n-gram speculator with variable-length drafts (#40704), Elastic EP (#53934), pipeline parallelism with prefill context parallelism for MLA models (#59139), a stock torch.compile mode (#59079), and MRV2 is now the default on ROCm with the model-specific MRV1 exceptions removed (#56360).
Faster startup and serving: vllm download-kernels installs FlashInfer's precompiled kernels (#58765); vllm preload --preload-autotune keeps the FlashInfer autotune table warm across restarts (#60085); a shared-memory tensor arena broadcasts large multimodal tensors to workers with one copy (#51207); tokenizers and processors load from the local snapshot (#60825); and with --api-server-count above 1 each connection goes to the least-loaded API worker, for 43-85% more req/s on short requests (Qwen3-0.6B, 32 input / 1 output tokens) in th

data.author: github-actions[bot]

MiMo V2.6
Xiaomi MiMo's mimo-v2.6, a 9B model built for code and agent workflows, is now supported in Ollama.
sh
ollama run mimo-v2.6
AutoTrust decision models
AutoTrust decision models read text and return choices, yes or no probabilities, and ratings for the questions you supply. The family includes 9b, 35b, and 27b-vl sizes — the 35b and 27b-vl sizes can also read images.
sh
ollama run autotrust-jev "A customer says their card was charged twice." --ask "Is this a billing issue?"
Note: autotrust-jev is supported on Apple silicon in this release.
What's Changed
ollama launch now supports Kimi Code CLI — the successor to kimi-cli — and offers to migrate existing kimi-cli setups
ollama launch now fills in Pi's model list automatically so models can be picked inside Pi, and Claude Desktop's model
picker shows Ollama's actual model names
Recurrent and vision GGUF models can now serve more than one request at a time
Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 models using long-context (YaRN) scaling
Running ollama with no arguments opens the welcome launcher

data.title: open-webui/open-webui v0.13.1
data.author: github-actions[bot]
data.summary:
Added
🦾 Coding agents as models. On an Open Terminal that offers agents, coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Pi now appear in the model picker. You can chat with them or call them by voice, choose their reasoning effort and service tier, and approve their tool requests in the chat. Each conversation uses one agent, and agent chats cannot be regenerated, continued or edited and resent. If an agent's terminal goes away, its chats and new chats fall back to the default model and earlier replies keep the agent's name. Autocompletion in agent chats uses the task model, or is skipped when there is none. #33843, #33860, #33880, #33857
🪢 Introducing Tether. Tether is the new desktop companion app for macOS, Windows and Linux that ties your own computer to Open WebUI. Sign in once and your computer shows up under Your devices in the terminal menu, so models, coding agents and automations can work in your real files, repositories and tools, and you can reach them from any browser, including your phone. Tether connects out to Open WebUI, so there are no ports to open, its terminal output resumes after a dropped connection, and it delivers notifications to your desktop even when no Open WebUI page is open. It signs in with a renewable session that expires after 90 days without use by default, set with "SESSIONEXPIRESIN".
💸 Much cheaper tool chats. Chats that use tools now cost much less. Citation instructions, memory recall, the skills list and attached knowledge are no longer rewritten into the system prompt or your message on every tool round, so the start of the conversation stays the same between requests and providers can serve it from their prompt cache. Custom pipes see a different message layout as a result; see Context as hidden tool results under Changed. #33852
